tickets.title: JovraStudioCore contracts: Codable models for every jovra.* Studio schema, canonical JSON and a manifest test that fails on an unconsumed fixture
tickets.what_to_build: STU-01. JovraStudioCore reads and writes every Studio contract: project-lock, source-manifest, sync-map, observation, keeper and B-roll catalogs, story-profile catalog, story-brief, edit-plan/2, reference-catalog, render-job, quote, usage-reservation, delivered-artifact, lesson, camera-invite, storage-providers, plus the contract data files (story-profiles.v1.json, render-job-transitions.v1.json, credit-classes.v1.json). Decoders are strict (unknown fields and integral floats refused, as the reference does), ids and hashes are checked with ECMA-262 pattern semantics (a value ending in a newline is refused even though the core Python gate still accepts it, SOF-R4-02, which stays open for the core gate owner), canonical re-encoding reuses core T03's canonical JSON writer and is byte-identical to the fixtures, and time values use exact rationals and integer microseconds (SD7) with the one half-up rounding function. Record round-trips are registry-driven: each schema id maps to a decoder registered by the Swift module that owns it, so later tickets register their own decoders in their own folders. A manifest test enumerates spec/studio/fixtures (records, invalid and vectors; fixtures/media belongs to the media package tests) and reads each module page's front matter: a kind whose page says `swift: consumed` must be consumed by a registered Swift test, a kind whose page says `swift: pending` may be unconsumed, and a kind or schema in no page fails. There is no shared allow-list file: each later Swift ticket flips only its own module page's status line, so parallel tickets never edit the same file, and a spec ticket that adds a kind (S56, S68) lands it as pending. This ticket flips the records page to consumed. Why blocked: S03 (module pages carry the swift consumption status the manifest test reads); S04 (the package exists); T03 (canonical JSON, pct and provenance models in JovraCore are reused, not copied).
acceptance_criteria: Every record under spec/studio/fixtures/records whose schema has a registered decoder decodes and re-encodes byte-identically (count printed by the test, never asserted as a literal).
Every schema-layer invalid case for a registered schema is refused by the Swift decoder; the id/hash trailing-newline cases are refused even though Python `re.search` would accept them (finding 6).
An integral float (744.0) in a frame field and an unknown property are refused (negative tests).

SOF-R4-02 remains listed as open in the register (this ticket does not close it) and the PR links the core-owner issue for the core gate fix.
